newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen volatile, wary of Dow gains.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen volatile, wary of Dow gains.

text.p: German shares were seen remaining volatile over the coming week as they continued to look out for, albeit with growing suspicion, any further progress on Wall Street.
The IBIS-DAX electronic trade index stood just 2.19 points higher at 3,363.99 by 1323 GMT as overall volumes stayed thin.
"Nobody is trusting the gains on Wall Street anymore," said one trader, noting widespread expectations of a further U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase in May.
He added that the German market might as a result underperform any new gains made among U.S. shares.
The U.S. market was on Friday expected to push higher at the start, led by high-tech stocks after a better-than-expected third quarter report by Microsoft.
Within the DAX, drugs and chemicals group Hoechst saw the highest volume, easing 12 pfennigs to 64.23 after weakness on Thursday following a poorly-received presentation to British institutionals.
Dealers said earlier market rumours the group would issue a profit warning were now being discounted.
In the same sector, Bayer shed five pfennigs to 69.40 on relatively strong volume.

In the auto sector, Daimler-Benz AG lost 1.05 marks to 131.30 and BMW AG was down 15.50 marks at 1,391.50 marks. Dealers said the drop was more of a correction than the start of a trend, adding there was a still a degree of bullishness surrounding the stocks.
